subject: pulse-oximeter + glucometer
championNote: The map earns its bytes when the bare rung has visibly LOST SURFACE, and not when the bare rung already reads correct. pulse-oximeter bare is melted and the map recovers it for 1.1 MB; glucometer bare already reads near-reference and the map buys almost nothing for 985 KB. This also explains #694: the shoe's 60k bare already read correct so the map was waste, and the shoe's 40k bare was melted but the map cannot repair an OUTLINE, only shading. Surface loss is repairable by a map; silhouette loss is not.
formPredictionOutcome: PREDICTIONS RECORDED BEFORE BAKES. All four rungs predicted holds_silhouette on the FORM basis: boxy subjects go deep, curved subjects do not. pulse-oximeter is the case the stage was built for (296,226 raw to 25,000 plus a 512 map held at 12.6% under its shipped 80k champion in the hand-run); glucometer is the boxy handheld that held at 25k on FORM grounds. The map shades facets and cannot move a silhouette, so the mapped variant carries the same prediction as the bare one. FORM stands at 3 of 4 after #694; a wrong prediction here is a real miss for the record and fails nothing in this sweep's contract. OUTCOME: 4 of 4 correct on this sweep — all four rungs predicted holds_silhouette and all four held. FORM moves to 7 of 8 overall, its one miss still being lowpoly-shoe 60k bare.

byteContext.note: bytes are recorded, not ranked — the render is the only oracle. shipped80kReferenceBytes = the shipped 80k champion GLB per subject (champion.glb in each subject's optimize dir). Percentages in any future graded verdict are vs these cells.

formPredictorBasis: FORM at 3 of 4 after #694: correct for 40k bare, 40k mapped and 60k mapped on lowpoly-shoe; WRONG for 60k bare, which held its silhouette and beat the shipped asset. Every FORM failure so far is on the curved side. Both subjects here are boxy handhelds, which is the class that has held at 25k before — glucometer 1 for 1, pulse-oximeter by hand at 37.82 map deviation as resolution fell from 2048.
bakeStage: tools/openclinxr/asset-pipeline/trellis/iterate-optimize.ts --bake --bake-res 512 --target <25k low rung> (hl_bake.py high-to-low, export_mapped.py attach, ab_render.py grade PNG)

rungs.subject: pulse-oximeter
rungs.verdictNote: Silhouette holds — the boxy FORM prediction is correct here. But the surface reads melted against the reference: the screen bezel is simplified, the button collapses to a rounded blob, the finger-slot pad loses its texture, and the parting-line groove softens to a shallow wave with its shadow line gone. Distinguishable from the 80k reference at native without cropping.

rungs.subject: pulse-oximeter
rungs.verdictNote: The map restores what the bare rung lost — bezel crisp, button a defined block, finger-pad texture back, body edges sharp — at 12.6% under the shipped champion. This reproduces the hand-run figure to the byte (8,682,420), so the stage does what the hand script did. RESIDUAL DEFECT, recorded rather than waived: the parting seam carries jagged dark and light streaks absent from the reference at the same 1:1 crop, the same contamination class as the shoe heel collar. It is a narrow band and I judged the surface recovery worth it at this saving; a re-bake above 512 should be tried before this is adopted anywhere.

rungs.subject: glucometer
rungs.verdictNote: Reads close to the 80k reference — panel lines, button edges, bezel and strip slot all present, with only a marginally softer bezel and slightly rounder body corners. 20.5% under the shipped champion with no artifact. Nothing here needed a map.

rungs.subject: glucometer
rungs.verdictNote: Marginally crisper bezel and panel edges than the bare rung, and no visible contamination. But it costs 985,312 bytes more than the bare rung — 11.3% — for a gain the bare rung already delivers. Against the bare 25k it loses on cost at near-equal appearance, so the map does not earn its bytes on this subject.

referenceRenders.note: 80k shipped champion per subject rendered with the same renderer, no map — the known-good column. Not a rung (it is the graded upper endpoint), so it is not in rungs[] and cannot be the champion.

notEvidenceFor: that any variant is adoptable — every verdict is inconclusive_blocked pending the orchestrator's pixel grade and nothing here asserts a ready-to-ship claim
that the bake stage's 512 default resolution suits boxy subjects — the hand-run pulse-oximeter evidence swept 2048 downward and this sweep fixes nothing about it
that a map winning or losing on these two subjects generalises to boxy subjects as a class — two subjects cannot establish that
that the heel-collar contamination seen on both mapped shoe rungs is absent here — whether it appears on a boxy subject is exactly what the renders are for
contaminationObserved: Jagged streaks at a concave seam on pulse-oximeter 25k mapped, absent from its 80k reference at the same 1:1 crop. Same class as the lowpoly-shoe heel collar on both mapped rungs. NOT observed on glucometer 25k mapped. Three mapped variants across two subjects now show it, one does not; it is unmeasured whether concavity is the common factor.
